subject: Draft: Success profiles, exit signals & acceptance tests for evaluation
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medcorehealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: Success profiles, exit signals & acceptance tests for evaluation

Lena —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Per our conversation, I put together a short draft that frames the mutual action plan (MAP) for the 4-week evaluation: primary success profiles, concrete exit gates, and the acceptance tests we'll run. Attached: MAP_template_v2.xlsx and a short Eval-Test-Cases.md with runnable checks.

High level (summary):
- Goal: Validate Redwood's hosted inference for patient-note summarization at target latency and precision while ensuring no PHI is retained outside your VPC (if you choose Dedicated/Private).
- Success profiles (pass/fail):
  1) Latency SLO: 95th percentile <= 350ms for 512-token prompts under a sustained 20 rps load.
  2) Quality SLO: ROUGE-L >= 0.62 and human QA pass rate >= 90% on a 200-record QA set (sample provided).
  3) Security: No external storage of raw notes; audit logs visible for every inference call.
- Exit gates (must be green to move to pilot):
  A) Latency gate satisfied for 3 consecutive weekdays under realistic traffic patterns.
  B) Quality gate satisfied + no critical QA regressions.
  C) Security checklist items 1–4 completed and validated by your InfoSec.
- Acceptance tests (examples):
  • Load test harness (script + dataset) — measures p95 token latency and tail behavior.
  • Adversarial prompt set — measures hallucination rate and PII exposure.
  • KV cache / state consistency — ensures session continuity for multi-turn summarization.

Proposed close timeline (if all gates pass):
- Week 0 (this week): Confirm MAP and access to eval environment.
- Week 1: Baseline tests and initial tuning.
- Week 2–3: Full QA, load, and security validation.
- Week 4: Signoff and contract SOW/commit (if green).

Next steps: Please review the attached MAP and the test-case doc. If the items above look right, can we lock in a kickoff on Monday (Nov 2) at 10am PT so my infra lead can provision the evaluation environment?

Attachments: MAP_template_v2.xlsx (worksheet: Success-Metrics), Eval-Test-Cases.md

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medcorehealth.com>

Cc: Ben Kim <ben.kim@medcorehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 12:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Draft: Success profiles, exit signals & acceptance tests for evaluation

Thanks, Aditya — this is helpful. A few clarifying notes from our side:

- The quality metric you suggested (ROUGE-L >= 0.62) seems reasonable as an initial target, but our clinical reviewers will evaluate edge cases. Can you add a short plan for how human QA will be sampled and scored? We want the sampling to include rare-terminology notes.
- For security, we need explicit confirmation that no PHI leaves our VPC during the evaluation. Which deployment option will satisfy that (Dedicated vs Private)?
- Timeline: Nov 2 kickoff is OK, but procurement needs a mutual action item for DocuSign of an evaluation addendum (NDA + eval scope). Can you share a draft?

Also, Ben (cc) will own procurement/contracting — Ben, do you have any immediate questions on agreement terms for a 4-week eval?

-Lena
Director of Clinical Computing
MediCore Health
lena.ortiz@medcorehealth.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medcorehealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: Success profiles, exit signals & acceptance tests for evaluation

Lena — great questions, thanks. Quick answers inline and I've updated the attached Eval-Test-Cases.md with the sampling plan and the propos ed human QA rubric.

- Human QA sampling: we propose stratified sampling across 4 buckets (common notes, rare-terminology, adversarial prompts, de-identified corner cases). The rubric has a 1–5 scale for factuality, completeness, and safety; pass = average >= 4 across the set. We will provide the 200-record seed sample and anonymize where required.
- PHI and deployment options: Dedicated and Private both support keeping data inside your VPC. For a Hosted eval we can enable network restrictions and token redaction, but for strict PHI non-exfiltration only Dedicated (reserved capacity in your VPC) or Private on-prem will be acceptable. If you want us to run the eval with zero PHI leaving your network, we recommend Dedicated.
- DocuSign addendum: attached SLA_draft_MediCore.pdf which includes an evaluation addendum template (page 2). We can provision a DocuSign link as soon as procurement confirms address and signatory.

Proposed updates to MAP (high level):
1) Add human QA sampling + rubric (attached).
2) Add a procurement milestone for DocuSign sign-off no later than end of Week 1.
3) Add an InfoSec validation window (48 hours) after we complete the security checklist.

Can Grace and Marissa confirm infra and product commitments for Week 1? We need a named point of contact for on-call support during load tests.

Thanks,
Aditya

Lena / Aditya —

We can cover the infra and on-call for Week 1. Quick commitments:
- I will be primary on-call for provisioning (Grace O'Connor). Contact: grace@redwoodinference.com / +1 (650) 555-0116.
- Marissa will take ownership of the QA rubric execution and model tuning knobs.
- We'll provision a Dedicated eval environment scoped to your test data (if you confirm the Dedicated route). It typically takes 24–48 hours to reserve GPUs and network peering.

Notes on acceptance tests:
- Load tests: we'll run the provided harness against a mirrored dataset with realistic concurrency and produce a p95 report, plus an artifact with raw traces.
- Adversarial prompts: we'll run your adversarial set and our internal safety checks; any critical safety failures will trigger stop-and-investigate and pause the eval until fixed.

Action items:
- Lena: confirm Dedicated vs Hosted for the eval (Dedicated preferred for PHI).
- Ben: can procurement sign the evaluation addendum by Friday (Nov 5)?

Happy to discuss during the Nov 2 kickoff.

-Grace
